title: Oklahoma 77, Texas A&M 0: The Big 12 Record Rout of 2003
question: What was the score of Oklahoma's 2003 game against Texas A&M?
answer: Oklahoma beat Texas A&M 77-0 on November 8, 2003, in Norman. The margin was a Big 12 record and the worst loss in Aggies football history.
summary: On Nov. 8, 2003, No. 1 Oklahoma beat Texas A&M 77-0 in Norman, a Big 12 record margin and the worst loss in Aggies history. Here are the details.
body: Oklahoma hosts Texas A&M this Saturday, so it is a good week to revisit the most one-sided meeting between the two programs. On November 8, 2003, the top-ranked Sooners beat the Aggies 77-0 in Norman.

Oklahoma came in unbeaten and left 10-0 overall and 6-0 in the Big 12. Texas A&M fell to 4-6. The Aggies' own athletics site called it their worst loss ever, and the Lawrence Journal-World reported it as the worst defeat in 108 years of A&M football.

The numbers were lopsided. According to the A&M report, Oklahoma gained 636 yards to the Aggies' 54, and A&M drew more penalty yards than it gained on offense. Quarterback Jason White tied a school record with five touchdown passes, and receiver Mark Clayton caught three of them to push his single-season Oklahoma touchdown total to 12.
The margin was a Big 12 record, and the 77 points tied the conference mark for points in a game. It was also Oklahoma's most lopsided win since a 77-0 victory over Missouri in 1986.

Bob Stoops said afterward the situation felt odd to him and, according to the Journal-World, called four straight runs up the middle late to keep it from growing. Texas A&M now meets Oklahoma as a fellow SEC member, a very different setting from that Norman afternoon.
